findings.title: Prostration as embodied reversal
findings.claim: Under the reminder, falling and prostration enact the bodily opposite of self-exalting refusal: the signs bring the body low rather than allowing the self to keep a superior height.
findings.mechanism: The focus joins خَرُّوا and سُجَّدًا to the denial of استكبار. In 2:34, Iblis refuses the command to prostrate and is explicitly described as arrogant. That wider contrast makes the focus's downward bodily response legible as a reversal of resistant self-elevation rather than an isolated posture.
findings.reader_payoff: Prostration reads not only as an accompanying rite but as a bodily refusal to claim height over the sign.
findings.containment: The 2:34 connection supplies exact Arabic but no target morphology; the opposition is contextual, not an etymology or a claim that every use of prostration means humility. The focus itself does not name Iblis.

epistemic.reason: The cross-run claim is well anchored in focus branches and the exact 2:34 wording; its wider inverse relation remains interpretive, and the represented legacy reading receives the same qualification.

findings.mechanism: The focus's سَبَّحُوا۟ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّهِمْ joins distancing God from deficiency to positive praise. The wider formula in 39:75 repeats glorification-with-hamd and is followed by judgment in truth and the final praise to God. This makes evaluative recognition perceptible while the focus's sequence shows that bodily yielding continues into speech.
findings.reader_payoff: The response is both bodily and discerning: it lowers the self, clears false attribution, and positively recognizes what is praiseworthy.
findings.containment: The focus does not itself mention final judgment, angels, or a chronological aftermath. 39:75 supplies a resonant scene, not a claim that 32:15 occurs after that judgment; the tested-praise facet remains an interpretive extension.

epistemic.reason: The conventional praise branches are well supported and the paired formula is exact in 39:75; reading judgment as an evaluative trigger is a contextual inference. One represented legacy claim adds the fall-to-speech relation.

findings.title: Signs become an embodied response

The wider recitation scenes in 19:58 and 25:73 make prostration legible as one response to signs, contrasted with a deaf-blind refusal, while 32:9 recalls that possession of faculties alone does not ensure gratitude.
findings.mechanism: The focus's visible signs and reminder precede falling and prostration. In 19:58, recited signs are followed by falling prostrate and weeping; 25:73 describes a different response when reminded by signs, explicitly denying a deaf-blind fall. The earlier 32:9 account of hearing, sight, hearts, and little gratitude sharpens the difference between receiving faculties and answering a reminder.
findings.reader_payoff: Faith appears as successful transmission from perception through recollection into posture, not mere exposure to evidence.
findings.containment: The comparisons are contextual echoes, not a universal causal law. The connection targets provide exact Arabic but no target morphology; 25:73 is not reduced to a simple lexical opposite, and 32:9 is outside the declared pericope.

epistemic.reason: A legacy support nominates the sequence; exact focus branches and supplied Arabic in the wider anchors support the surface contacts, while the conversion chain remains an inference.

findings.mechanism: The focus's glorification and hamd meet Rabb, whose registered nurturing branch supplies formative care. In 32:9 the Lord fashions the human and breathes life; 39:75 closes judgment with glorification and praise; 2:34 joins refusal to prostrate with arrogance. Together these contexts activate the legacy reading of praise as an evaluative verdict that does not compete for greatness.

epistemic.reason: The candidate is an unbound reader interpretation. Its named focus branches are registered, and the context texts are exact in the packet, but their combination into a tested verdict is inferential.

findings.title: Faith as a whole-person circuit
findings.claim: The focus can be read as a complete response circuit: signs and reminder move into belief, bodily lowering and prostration, then spoken praise. In 8:2 mention and recitation unsettle hearts, increase faith, and lead to reliance; 19:58 likewise joins recited signs to prostration, while 40:7 pairs angelic glorification with praise and belief.
findings.mechanism: The restrictive إِنَّمَا and temporal إِذَا frame an event sequence in the focus. The wider passages repeat portions of that chain: 8:2 moves from mention and recitation to heart and faith, 19:58 from recitation to prostration, and 40:7 from glorification-with-hamd to belief and intercession. These parallels make faith a transmission through the whole person rather than bare exposure.
findings.reader_payoff: The verse's bodily and verbal clauses become the observable completion of faith, not material appended after an inward state.
findings.containment: The full circuit is an inferred relation among passages, not an explicit formula stated in any one of them. Connection targets are supplied as exact Arabic without target morphology; the focus does not say that every believer displays every external response in the same way.

epistemic.reason: The candidate is a legacy synthesis of focus syntax and branches; the wider Arabic supplies exact thematic parallels, but the circuit itself is interpretive.

findings.title: The fall in a wider vertical relay
findings.claim: The believer's fall can be read as a bodily receiving point in a wider descent-and-return pattern: revelation descends in 32:2, the managed order ascends in 32:5, the focus body yields, and its praise moves the received response onward.
findings.mechanism: The exact wider contexts supply descent and ascent; the focus supplies a downward bodily response and a praise verb whose root inventory also carries a flowing-motion branch. Together they form a reader-inferred vertical relay in which reception becomes returned praise.
findings.reader_payoff: The fall is no longer only lowering before an already-arrived message; it becomes the embodied junction where received guidance is answered and carried onward.
findings.containment: The relation is not stated as a causal chain, and the alternative that 32:2, 32:5, and 32:15 describe independent acts under divine governance remains live. The context roots are unresolved HFT nominations. The focus's Form II tasbih remains ordinary glorification; the flowing-motion branch is analogical, not a literal gloss.

epistemic.reason: The HFT trace supplies exact context ayahs, word positions, roots, attributed roles, and a return to registered focus carriers, but its relay is explicitly reader-inferred and its source is legacy_unbound.

findings.mechanism: HFT-attributed context branches nominate doubt, wavering, and fixed knowledge; the focus contributes registered security and remembering branches. When those contacts are read together, faith changes from an opposite opinion into a process of settling after reminder.
findings.reader_payoff: A reminder can be perceived as re-centering a wavering person, not only as supplying another proposition.
findings.containment: The root mapping at 32:23 to undulation is non-dominant and unresolved; all context branches remain attributed. The simpler reading—ordinary doubt opposed to certainty without a dynamic process—is preserved, and no psychological or physical mechanism is asserted as fact.

findings.title: Received growth is not self-inflation
findings.claim: The focus need not imply shrinking the self: 32:9 presents life and faculties as received, while the focus praises the Lord's nurturing and rejects self-exaltation. The contrast is between growth received from its source and enlargement claimed by the self.
findings.mechanism: The context's breathing and life-bearing spirit branches are attributed from 32:9; the focus supplies registered nurturing and self-superiority branches. Their meeting distinguishes received vitality from the prideful inflation nominated in the same wider HFT trace.
findings.reader_payoff: Humility can allow full vitality while refusing to misattribute its source; the problem is self-authored superiority, not growth itself.
findings.containment: The inflation and spirit mappings remain unresolved HFT attributions; the Rabb root's nurturing branch is a registered possibility, not a claim that Rabb lexically means biological growth here. The live alternative is ordinary gratitude for creation, and the comparison is inferential.

epistemic.reason: Exact Arabic at both anchors and registered focus branches support contact, but all context branch mappings are attributed and the received-versus-appropriated distinction is an HFT inference.

findings.mechanism: The same focus objects—reminder, signs, and Lord—recur in 32:22, but the response changes to turning away. This controlled mirror makes low submission a way of facing the claim and the turned side a spatial image of evasion; the HFT also links self-magnification to preserving distance.
findings.reader_payoff: Non-arrogance gains a bodily direction: one is available to the sign instead of protecting a flank from it.
findings.containment: The focus does not literally say 'face' or 'side'; the spatial relation is contextual and inferred. The target Arabic supplies no independent branch gloss for turning aside, so that HFT branch remains attributed. The simpler contrast of obedience and disobedience without spatial force remains viable.

findings.title: Human prostration in a creation-wide submission
findings.claim: The focus's prostrating believers can be situated as a human instance of a wider creation-wide submission: 16:49 says that creatures and angels in the heavens and earth prostrate to God and are not arrogant.
findings.mechanism: The focus supplies human prostration and a denial of self-exaltation; 16:49 repeats both prostration and the absence of arrogance across the heavens, earth, creatures, and angels. That explicit pairing widens the act's scale without erasing its human voluntariness in the focus.
findings.reader_payoff: The believers' lowered posture appears within a cosmic field of submission, not as a private gesture detached from creation.
findings.containment: 16:49 describes universal creaturely and angelic prostration, not necessarily the same chosen human act; the connection verifies exact wording but supplies no target morphology. The scale analogy does not make all creatures' submission identical to human ritual.

epistemic.reason: The connection's exact Arabic directly supports the prostration-and-no-arrogance pairing; the placement of the human act as an instance within that wider field is interpretive.
